relevance.rationale: Computes the real part of the semi-classical limit of the sequence of quantum hyperbolic invariants of the figure-eight knot complement and shows it is rigid — independent of the choice of holonomy representation — and equal either to 0 or to the hyperbolic volume of the complement divided by 2*pi, according to a parity condition on the logarithms of the holonomy eigenvalues along the canonical longitude. The figure-eight complement is the single most load-bearing manifold in this folio: Vol(4_1) is the muon anchor (m_mu/m_e = Vol(4_1)/hbar_q^2, i.e. the numerical proxy that pins the CAL-2 modulus), and the corpus carries the volume conjecture only as an axiomatised Lean class (conj:kashaev-volume-conjecture, QOU.Kashaev.VolumeConjecture) with kashaev1997 as its sole literature input. A rigorous volume-limit theorem for exactly this complement is therefore directly on the corpus's critical path. Two honest caveats which are the reason I am not proposing aid-proof: the invariants computed here are quantum hyperbolic invariants, not the Kashaev/colored-Jones invariant the corpus's class axiomatises, and the limit is 0 OR Vol/(2 pi) depending on a parity condition, so it is a conditional identification, not an unconditional discharge.

keyResults.locator: Abstract; Theorem 1.1 and its triangulation version (section 1.2)
keyResults.statement: The real part of the semi-classical limit of the quantum hyperbolic invariants of the figure-eight knot complement is rigid (independent of the holonomy representation chosen) and equals 0 or Vol/(2*pi) according to a parity condition on the logarithms of the holonomy eigenvalues on the canonical longitude.
keyResults.useForFolio: The nearest published theorem to the corpus's axiomatised volume conjecture, on the exact manifold the CAL-2 anchor uses; it also supplies a rigidity statement (no dependence on the holonomy choice) that the corpus's anchor implicitly assumes.

proposedActions.rationale: Core and orphan; the corpus's volume-conjecture class currently rests on kashaev1997 alone.

Record the epistemic status honestly: a rigid semi-classical volume limit is proved for the figure-eight complement, for the quantum hyperbolic invariants and subject to a parity condition. What would need checking before it could touch the Lean class: whether the invariants here and the Kashaev invariant the class axiomatises are the same object at the relevant limit, and whether the parity condition holds at the corpus's chosen longitude/logarithm branch. Until both are settled this is a scope statement, never a discharge of the conjecture.
